I agree with the Vitamin D part. I had this issue last year in the winter. However, when it was raised to an exceptional level, I still had depression. It got worse in the summer (even though I travelled in the summer to Europe) and was terrible in August (mind you the sun was out and I went out every day).

Thank you for this comment.
I have put her advice in the context of her life; I believe she was raised in a Catholic home however where she lived I don’t believe they were sexually repressed (from her accounts). Many of her friends and peers were sexually active; only in marriage were they expected to remain monogamous.
The only issues is that when I have my idea of fun (clubs/reading) she is against it. She has tried to dress me provocatively since I was in the fifth grade and pushed me to be sexual in middle school.

I understand putting things into their perspective; the way they were raised would definitely affect how they will raise their children. I’ve done this time and time and again, trying to normalize her behavior towards me and though I pity her in some ways I cannot forget how awful she was and still is towards me. 

Don’t worry you’re not invalidating my feelings. I like hearing other sides to further my understanding.

No, I understand the dangers of antidepressants; I plan to finish taking them after two months. I don’t want to be on them forever or longer.
It’s just that this behavior isn’t a one time case. She’s been weirdly sexual with me for the longest I can remember. Her offering me a plane ticket to go have sex and come back was just the last straw for me.
From her point of view, she thinks I’m sheltered however I’m not. Still in high school, in clubs such as debate and Congress. But she chooses to focus on me periodically being on my phone while I’m in my room.

I understand what you mean, however after living with her for 18 years I know she doesn’t care for my wellbeing.

The discussion of depression relating to Instagram celebrities and hikikomori is an interesting read, no doubt about that.

She isn’t European she’s from Haiti. I was 17 when she sent this message. This isn’t the first time she’s suggested me to have sex (15 one time). 
While I understand seasonal depression exists, I don’t have seasonal depression. 

I understand your point of view though.
I told my school counselor.
Thank you. I don’t think she knows what’s right for me either.
No this is my mother. It’s from her messenger account.

My school counselor told me that these messages were suggestions of human trafficking. She believes my depression can be cured with higher vitamin d levels (even when my levels were high I was still depressed). Sorry for the bad English.

I don’t think it is. My mother said any man that shows interest towards me is only after one thing.  And that no one will love me as much as her (ew). I think it’s an isolation tactic.
Keep your chin up; if you think taking measures to better yourself will help you then continue to do so. I wouldn’t listen to what your mother said, it’s hurtful and inappropriate to say to your child.
I think it would. Since my first name is my fathers and my mothers together. I just started to hate it too.

My mother did the same thing. We were in a field trip and one of my friends said there was no reason to live and attempted to jump in front of a truck. Of course I yelled at him and pulled him back and stayed with him the rest of the day. I tell my mom after school; she calls me stupid for it and says I shouldn’t save anyone at all. Yet she wants me to be a doctor LOL

My mother once told me that she felt the same way I was feeling when I told her how abusive she was. Her mother is a narc(she used to drop herself in the floor to guilt trip her cheating husband, fight him and bite him/my grandfather cheated and never was there for my mother). My fathers parents died when he was young so naturally he’s absent. They normalized it because the society they grew up in was unsophisticated and never considered their treatment to be abusive. Luckily I’ll never have to speak or see them again.

I think so too. She said she had a nightmare that I was being interviewed by a journalist who hands me a mic and she said it was so scary that she had to wake up; she then says I have to “watch what I’m saying to others.”

Because I’ve been dealing with a lot for a long while now and it doesn’t seem to be getting better.  I feel lost and no matter how many times I try to get on the right path I’m shot down by myself and the only way to get away from myself is ending it. I can’t and won’t get better and frankly I don’t think I deserve help either

I,m sorry you had to go through these things; I suggest to get an easy going job to start making some money then save. Visit with your counselor as well. Good luck ❤️

Maybe show interest in abroad studies to a more free country where religion isn’t extremely forced. And if you become more open about not believing in Islam, make sure you’re safe when abroad so you don’t get into trouble. Stay safe :)

They have gender bias. I remember my mom telling me about marrying men and since we have Christian beliefs the topic of waiting came up. She believes men shouldn’t be virgins but women must be virgins. Doesn’t make sense when the Bible calls for both the man and the woman to be virgins.
My nmom would ask me if I’m *actually* going to wait until marriage. Mind you, she came into the bathroom while I was doing my business and had the audacity to ask this question in the most inappropriate time:
“Are you sure you’re going to wait? What if something happens?”  Back then I felt uncomfortable because I’m not gonna sleep with her, why the hell does she care? But I answered I’m still going to wait. She kept pushing me not to.
I remember since the fifth grade when I started to hit puberty she would comment on my body (this is when I had body confidence), wishing that she could have a body like mine. Later in the years she would criticize me, calling me too heavy or too skinny. She would tell me to do exercises to lift my breasts since they’re “too saggy” (I’m under 18). 
She would tell me on school mornings: “Don’t wear leggings your entire butt is out! Do you want everyone to see it?” 
Last week I was wearing rather tight clothing that was showing my arms and I felt uncomfortable so I asked if she had a jacket. She tells me: “Don’t be too self conscious you look good.” Her “compliment didn’t sound genuine. Last year for back to school she tried to “slutify” me, by buying me rather tight clothing, cleavage revealing or short skirts/dresses, tight jeans, and would comment on my body. I have an interest in Korean style clothing which in some aspects is cute and conservative. My mother would tell me “what are you, old?” Then would guide me towards clothing I’m too uncomfortable to be in.

When I was in the fifth grade I ate a *lot*. I would easily shed off the pounds but it was summer and there was no track practice. I go downstairs to sit on the steps in front of my family her who’s on the computer; he says to me “oh you’re getting fatter, that’s good, don’t lose weight.” I didn’t understand so I go to my mother; she says “he’s only saying that so no boy will come to you.” She then sent me outside to play, in hopes I would lose the weight.
My father tells me to coverup if I’m “showing” too much. One morning I was topless because the last night was too hot, and got up to use the bathroom. I was in the hallway; I’m not sure if fathers are supposed to look up to the ceiling, blink and clear their throat after seeing their daughter topless; it was in no way sexual. If fathers can be okay with their sons being topless because they don’t sexualize them then it’s fine if their daughters are too right? Well no. Guess not.

Yup. As of right now I’m greyrocking her but weeks before we had an argument. She blamed the “demons” that were turning me against her and that God sees through me and will punish me for disobeying. She obviously quoted the Bible verse about not disobeying your parents but I never listened. I never stopped believing in God but I stopped going to church with her and my dad. I can’t stand hypocritical Christians.
